newsitem.title: USA: NASA puts off U.S. shuttle landing.
newsitem.headline: NASA puts off U.S. shuttle landing.

text.p: The threat of fog forced NASA on Monday to postpone the planned homecoming of the space shuttle Discovery.
The $2 billion resuable spaceship was scheduled to land at Florida's Kennedy Space Center at 7:14 a.m. EDT (1114 GMT) but mission control said the chance of ground fog was too high.
"The probability of fog is too high to be acceptable," mission control's Dom Gorie told the crew.
There was only one opportunity to land in Florida on Monday and the shuttle's homecoming was rescheduled for 7:08 a.m. EDT (1108 GMT) on Tuesday.
NASA never considered sending the shuttle to the backup landing strip in California on Monday because of the additional cost of transporting the shuttle back to Florida.
Discovery's crew of six are to return with an atmospheric satellite carrying a bounty of data about the depletion of the earth's protective ozone layer.
